title: Conceal Your Intentions
summary: Keeping your intentions hidden prevents others from predicting and planning against you. By using mixed signals, false sincerity, and noble gestures, you create a smoke screen that intrigues people and builds your value. Honesty and predictability lower respect, whereas an uninterpretable face and blending in allow you to mislead opponents. However, overusing deception can make you predictable, so it must be used carefully.
example: A boy creates interest in a girl using mixed signals and jealousy.
A Persian man strengthens his army instead of immediately attacking, defying expectations.
A French army lets a fort get captured to easily defeat the opponent later.
Warlord Sellasi uses mixed signals to create ambiguity and defeat another warlord.
An American man deceives a millionaire using a familiar lodge as a smoke screen.
FD Roosevelt and the Rothschilds use uninterpretable faces to prevent prediction.
reversal: Overusing deception makes it noticed and predictable, allowing others to defend against you.
If a deception fails, it is better to own your deception and continue to own your strangeness to avoid losing value.
